jobs.title: Drift Wood #19 · Last Bell
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; CHLOE — aged 18, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders, oversized dark cardigan, a Discman on her belt with headphones around her neck, a folded-back paperback, reads while talking; GULLY — aged 19, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: School lets out for the year. Not the last time. It feels like it anyway. Panel 1: the front steps of a small-town high school on the last day of the year, students pouring out past three teenagers who sit on the steps not moving, a bell ringing, spruce behind (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE, GULLY). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: a teenage boy in an overcoat sitting on school steps with his chin on his knees watching a parking lot empty (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "One more year. Then this town will have to find someone else to underestimate.". Panel 3: a boy in a backwards cap standing and stretching on school steps, easy and content (in this panel: GULLY). Gully says "Tide's out at four. You coming?". Wood says "I have to begin the real work.". Gully says "Tide's out at four.". Panel 4: three teenagers walking away from a school in a line toward a distant bay on a bright June afternoon, small in the frame, black and white, no words (in this panel: GULLY, CHLOE, WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
